name: Global food prices
summary: FAO food price index 133.9 in October, below the 135 Alert line but up 5.9% on a year; next release due 4 Dec
state: The FAO Food Price Index averaged 133.9 points in October, down 1.2% on September but 5.9% above a year earlier (FAO via Bizcommunity, 6 Nov). The annual rise meets the Watch line while the index stays below 135. Indian rice exporters were bracing for possible new export curbs in early November (S&P Global), but no ban by several major exporters of a staple was found as of 25 Nov. The next FAO release is due on 4 Dec.
for_you: Households in import-dependent countries face food costs higher than a year ago. Shoppers may see continued pressure on staples and sugar.
rubric_hit: Watch: FAO index y/y +5.9% > +5%; index 133.9 below 135 Alert line

sources.title: Bizcommunity — Global food prices fall in October as sugar rises for fourth month
S&P Global — Indian rice exporters brace for possible curbs on 100% broken rice exports

why: Food prices drive inflation, hunger and political unrest; poorer countries spend up to half of income on food.
drivers: Harvests, weather, fertiliser and energy costs, export bans, conflict in breadbaskets.

rubric.alert: FFPI > 135, or multiple major exporters ban exports of a staple.
rubric.watch: FFPI 120–135, or y/y > +5%, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: FAO Food Price Index < 120 and y/y change < +5%.
